_: Written 2026-09-20 as one of two decisions authored from scratch to find out where writing a codebook is awkward - the one step of this pipeline with no tooling and no measurement. A battery charger: the charging loop, the sensors and the UI stay ordinary firmware; only 'how hard should we push charge right now' goes through a proven circuit. Bucketing sensor readings into the codes below is the firmware's job and is not proven here. cycles has three legal values in two bits, so code 3 is illegal and the circuit answers it with stop + review = 1 by construction.
name: charge-throttle
scene: A battery charger in a handheld device. It can push full current, drop to a slow trickle, or stop charging altogether. Heat and swelling damage cells permanently and can be dangerous; charging slowly is always safe but takes longer; stopping means the device does not charge at all.
question: How hard should the charger push right now?

temp.raw: cell temperature bucketed by the firmware

soc.raw: state of charge bucketed by the firmware

cable.raw: 1 when the cable identified itself as a rated fast-charge cable

values.0: an ordinary cable of unknown rating
values.1: a cable rated for fast charging

cycles.raw: how worn the cell is, bucketed from the charge-cycle count; there is no code 3

values.2: a worn cell near the end of its life

swelling.raw: 1 when the pack sensor reports deformation

values.1: the pack is swollen or deformed

rule: swelling == 1 || temp == 3 ? stop : (temp == 2 || soc == 3 || cable == 0 || cycles == 2 ? slow : full)
